ri_dance_hall_boulder.blurb: Dance Hall Boulder is the centerpiece of the Hillsdale Boulders, a small group of blocks tucked into the woods of the De Coppet Estate in Rhode Island. The main boulder stands roughly 18 feet tall, with an overhanging east side and a slab facing west. It holds a dozen bouldering problems, mostly between very easy and V2 with a single V4, which makes it a friendly stop for newer boulderers or anyone wanting a mellow session. Several other boulders sit nearby, mostly a short walk to the north.

ri_cirque_the.blurb: The Cirque is the main warm-up zone at Connors Farm, a bouldering area in Rhode Island. It has a dozen problems, with most falling between V0 and V3, plus a few stiffer lines in the V4 to V7 range and one V10 at the top end. Its easiest problem is considered an excellent introduction to the grade. After topping out on one of the Cirque problems, a short two-minute stroll over a low stone wall leads to a small overhang called Hawk's Nest, so the two can be combined in one outing.

ri_tuolumne_boulder.blurb: Tuolumne Boulder is a clean, undercut erratic in Lincoln Woods State Park, a few miles north of Providence. Around a dozen bouldering problems start at V2 and climb to V11, with a solid middle of V4 to V7 and a couple of very hard lines for the strong. Lincoln Woods is known for high-quality bouldering on sharply textured stone, and its season runs deep into winter on sunny days, so this boulder is worth a visit when the weather is cold and dry.

ri_tomato_boulder.blurb: Tomato Boulder is the central block of the Tomato Boulders, a cluster of boulders in Lincoln Woods, Rhode Island, set along the loop road just east of the main warm-up area. It offers a dozen bouldering problems, most of them between V0 and V3 with a heavy helping at V1, plus a couple of tougher lines at V5 and V7. That spread suits climbers building up through the grades, and it is an easy add-on to a day at the warm-up boulders.

ri_mines_of_moria_the.blurb: The Mines of Moria is a collection of jutting rocks zig-zagging behind the Quarry Boulder in Lincoln Woods, Rhode Island. It has twelve bouldering problems with an easy start at V0 and a hard end at V5, though the bulk sit between V3 and V4, making it a good spot for solid intermediate climbers. The blocks have some unusual features and a few sharper holds than you find elsewhere in the park.
